content: The test image shows a stem/petiole with grayish-white powdery/fuzzy growth along its length. The plant part is the stem. Based on the part index, I'll focus on stem candidates. The grayish dusty spore-like coating strongly suggests Gray Mold or Sclerotinia Timber Rot.

- Key feature: grayish-white fine dusty/powdery coating along the stem length

- **Phytophthora_Blight stem**: Dark collapsed stems — does not match

The fine gray-white powdery/dusty coating on the stem is most consistent with Gray Mold (Botrytis cinerea), which produces "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass" on infected stem tissue. No other stem-affecting candidate in this set produces this kind of gray spore coating.
